==English==
{{swp}}

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|en|aboot||Northumbrian}}
* {{qualifier|archaic}} [[abowt]]; {{qualifier|abbreviation}} [[a.]], {{qualifier|abbreviation}} [[ab.]],* {{qualifier|abbreviation}} [[abt.]]

===Etymology===
{{etymon|en|id=preposition|:inh|enm:aboute<id:preposition>|tree=1}}
Preposition and adverb from {{inh|en|enm|aboute}}, {{m|enm|abouten}}, from {{inh|en|ang|abūtan}},<ref name=WI3>{{R:MW3 1976|page=5}}</ref> {{m|ang|onbūtan}}, from {{af|ang|on|t1=in, on|būtan|t2=outside of|nocat=1}} (compare modern {{m+|en|but}}, {{m|en|bout}}),<ref name=SOED>{{R:SOED5|page=7}}</ref> itself from {{af|ang|be|t1=by|ūtan|t2=outside|nocat=1}};<ref name=OXF>{{R:OCD2|page=4}}</ref> equivalent to {{compound|nocat=1|en|on|be|out}} or {{compound|nocat=1|en|on|but}}. Cognate with {{cog|ofs|abûta|t=outside; except}}. Not related to {{m|en|bout|t=period of time}}

Adjective from {{inh|en|enm|about|pos=adverb}}.

===Preposition===
{{wikidata lexeme|L2459}}
{{en-head|prep}}

# In a circle around; all round; on every side of; on the outside of; around. {{defdate|from before 1150}}<ref name=SOED/>
#: {{ux|en|The snake was coiled '''about''' his ankle.}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare All's Well|text=So look '''about''' you; know you any here?}}
#*: Let not mercy and truth forsake thee: bind them '''about''' thy neck; write them upon the table of thine heart:
#* <!-- Round the outside of (in contrast to directly over, through, across, or into). -->{{quote-book|en|year=1843|author=Thomas Hobbes|title=The English Works of Thomas Hobbes of Malmesbury: The history of the Grecian war written by Thucydides; tr. by T. Hobbes|page=480
|text=Pagondas {{...}} sent two companies of horse secretly '''about''' the hill; whereby that wing of the Athenians which was victorious, apprehending upon their sudden appearing that they had been a fresh army, was put into affright:{{nb...}}}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1874|author=David Laing Purves|title=The English Circumnavigators: The Most Remarkable Voyages Round the World by English Sailors|publisher=London : W.P. Nimmo|page=214
|text={{...}} for they could not get '''about''' the cape, because the wind on this coast is commonly between the NW. and SW., which makes it very difficult getting to the westward; but they left four canoes with forty-six men at the cape,{{nb...}}}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1877|author=Alfred Tennyson|title=The Works of Alfred Tennyson, Poet Laureate ...|page=241
|text=The Roman soldier found Me lying dead, my crown '''about''' my brows, {{...}}}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1879|title=The Living Age|page=727
|text=She looked '''about''' her again, and at last there he was, descending the steep path toward the station. He was half a mile off, and before she could decide what to do, a train came up and stopped.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1886|author=Duncan Keith|title=A history of Scotland: civil and ecclesiastical from the earliest times to the death of David I, 1153|volume=1
|passage=Nothing daunted, the fleet put to sea, and after sailing '''about''' the island for some time, a landing was effected in the west of Munster.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1892|author=w:James Yoxall
|chapter=5|title=[http://openlibrary.org/works/OL10504990W The Lonely Pyramid]
|passage=The desert storm was riding in its strength; the travellers lay beneath the mastery of the fell simoom. {{...}} Roaring, leaping, pouncing, the tempest raged '''about''' the wanderers, drowning and blotting out their forms with sandy spume.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1900|author=William John Tossell|title=Reports of Cases Argued and Determined in the Ohio Circuit Courts...: Ohio Circuit Decisions|page=581
|text=There is no controversy {{...}} that the plaintiff {{...}} fell into the ditch and was severely injured; [and] that the defendant or its agents left no railing '''about''' the excavation : And it quite clearly appears that a person coming from the house of the plaintiff, as she did, to cross the pavement in front of her lot, could not see any light or other signal to warn her of danger{{nb...}}}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1905|title=The Delineator|page=258
|text=She looked '''about''' her. Desolation everywhere - on the dust-encrusted windows, on the discolored walls, the rotten planks of the floor, the fallen bricks of the fireplace - desolation utter and complete.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|date=2016-08-24|origyear=????|author=Johanna Spyri|title=Moni the Goat Boy and Other Stories: Moni the Goahout a Friend; The Little Runaway|publisher=anboco|isbn=9783736409415
|text=As soon as church was out a group of people gathered '''about''' her, all curious to hear how she was getting on with the boy.}}
# Over or upon different parts of; through or over in various directions; here and there in; to and fro in; throughout. {{defdate|from ca. 1150–1350}}<ref name=SOED/>
#: {{ux|en|Rubbish was strewn '''about''' the place.}}
#: {{ux|en|The children were running '''about''' the room.}}
#: {{ux|en|He was well known '''about''' town.}}
#* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Regained|book=1|page=3|lines=30–35|passage=[I]n likeneſs of a Dove / The Spirit deſcended, while the Fathers voice / From Heav'n pronounc'd him his beloved Son. / That heard the Adverſary, who roving ſtill / '''About''' the world, at that aſſembly fam'd / Would not be laſt, {{...}}}}
#* {{RQ:Macaulay History of England|passage=He had been known, during several years, as a small poet; and some of the most savage lampoons which were handed '''about''' the coffeehouses were imputed to him.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1598|author=William Shakespeare|title=Love's Labour's Lost
|passage=where lies thy pain? And where my liege's? all '''about''' the breast.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1849|author=Thomas Babington Macaulay Baron Macaulay|title=The History of England from the Accession of James the Second|page=153
|text=Some Roman Catholics '''about''' the court had, indiscreetly or artfully, told all, and more than all, that they knew. The Tory Churchmen waited anxiously for fuller information.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1857|author=George Borrow?|title=The Quarterly Review|page=488
|text=She travelled '''about''' the country with a donkey and cart, selling silk and linen goods. Her great stature enabled her to be her own protector, and any liberties which were attempted to be taken with herself or her wares were sure to be answered by a beating.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|date=2022-11-13|origyear=????|author=Edith Nesbit|title=The Collected Works of Edith Nesbit|publisher=DigiCat
|text={{...}} to wander '''about''' the old place, climb the old walls, and explore the old passages, always dreaming of the days when the castle was noisy with men-at-arms, and gay with knights and ladies.}}
# {{n-g|Indicates that something will happen very soon; indicates a plan or intention to do something.}}
## {{lb|en|with 'to' and verb infinitive}} ''See '''''[[about to]]'''''.''
## {{lb|en|with present participle|obsolete|or|dialect}} On the point or verge of.
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1866|title=A treatise on the law of suits by attachment in the United States|author=Charles Daniel Drake|pageurl=http://books.google.de/books?id=Igs-AAAAIAAJ&pg=PA80&lpg=PA80&dq=%22was+about+leaving%22&source=bl&ots=aQXMZaxYAu&sig=T2wNto6m-YO2kSAwyWV-SivvnUw&hl=en&sa=X&ei=YblHUKaUJc2LswbzkIHQDw&redir_esc=y#v=onepage&q=%22was%20about%20leaving%22&f=false|page=80
|passage=[It] was held, that the latter requirement was fulfilled by an affidavit declaring that "the defendant was '''about''' leaving the State permanently."}}
# [[concerning|Concerning]]; with regard to; on account of; on the subject of. {{defdate|from ca. 1150–1350}}<ref name=SOED/>
#: {{syn|en|apropos|as for|Thesaurus:about}}
#: {{ux|en|He talked a lot '''about''' his childhood.}}
#: {{ux|en|We must do something '''about''' this problem.}}
#: {{ux|en|He is very mad '''about''' all the pranks.}}
#*: Doe you meane to stoppe any of Williams wages, '''about''' the Sacke he lost the other day?
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1671|author=w:John Milton|title=w:Samson Agonistes
|passage=I already have made way / To some Philistian lords, with whom to treat / '''About''' thy ransom.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1856|author=w:Voltaire|title=w:Philosophical dictionary
|passage=There have been violent quarrels about '''whether''' the whole is greater than a part.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1858|author=Thomas Babington Macaulay|title=The History of England from the Accession of James the Second|page=13
|text=[It was doubtful that] twenty governments, divided by quarrels '''about''' precedence, quarrels '''about''' territory, quarrels '''about''' trade, quarrels '''about''' religion, could long act together in perfect harmony.}}
#* {{RQ:Trollope Framley Parsonage|passage="I'll tell you what, Fanny: she must have her way '''about''' Sarah Thompson. You can see her to-morrow and tell her so."}}
#* {{RQ:Lincoln Pratt's Patients|chapter=4|passage=I told him '''about''' everything I could think of; and what I couldn't think of he did. He asked about six questions during my yarn, but every question had a point to it. At the end he bowed and thanked me once more. As a thanker he was main-truck high; I never see anybody so polite.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2008|author=Sean O'Neill|title=Cultural Contact and Linguistic Relativity Among the Indians of Northwestern California|publisher=University of Oklahoma Press|isbn=9780806139227|page=31
|text=Lucy Thompson, a Yurok woman who wrote a book '''about''' her experiences in the early twentieth century, reported that bilingualism was especially common at the religious dances, where neighboring groups often poured in from distant villages speaking utterly different languages.}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-06-22|volume=407|issue=8841|page=70
|title=[http://www.economist.com/news/finance-and-economics/21579879-buy-out-firm-really-does-focus-operational-improvements-engineers Engineers of a different kind]
|passage=Private-equity nabobs bristle at being dubbed mere financiers. Piling debt onto companies’ balance-sheets is only a small part of what leveraged buy-outs are '''about''', they insist. Improving the workings of the businesses they take over is just as core to their calling, if not more so. Much of their pleading is public-relations bluster.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|date=2013-09-05|author=Simon Gray|title=The Complete Smoking Diaries|publisher=Granta Books|isbn=9781847088666
|text=... look at it properly, her hands are the worst thing '''about''' her, visibly, anyway - they're filthy, as are the fingernails, broken and jagged and dark yellow from nicotine, the nicotine stain seems to go right into the palm{{nb...}}}}
#*: Well, let’s not talk '''about''' yesterday.
#* {{quote-book|en|date=2016-10-14|author=David J. Leonard|author2=Kimberly B. George|author3=Wade Davis|title=Football, Culture and Power|publisher=Taylor & Francis|isbn=9781317410898|page=187
|text=[F]ootball is '''about''' more than making plays on the field. It is '''about''' making them off the field as well. Our commitment to fans and the communities that support us does not end when the final seconds tick off the game clock {{...}} }}
#* {{quote-book|en|date=2021-10-07|author=Erica S. Simmons|author2=Nicholas Rush Smith|title=Rethinking Comparison: Innovative Methods for Qualitative Political Inquiry|publisher=Cambridge University Press|isbn=9781108967082|page=272
|text=... something particularly imaginative '''about''' comparative work, however one construes the term “comparison.”{{nb...}}}}
# [[concern|Concerned]] or occupied with; engaged in; [[intent]] on. {{defdate|from ca. 1150–1350}}<ref name=SOED/>
#: {{co|en|just going '''about''' their business}}
#: {{uxi|en|Have you much hay '''about?'''|Have you much in the process of making?<ref name="Holland"/>|q=Chester}}
#: {{uxi|en|“What’s Mary doin'?” “Oh! oo’s '''about''' th’ butter.”|“What’s Mary doing?” “Oh, she’s making the butter.”<ref name="Holland"/>|q=Chester}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1765|author=James HARRIS (Author of “Hermes.”.)|title=Hermes, Or a Philosophical Inquiry Concerning Universal Grammar ... Second Edition, Etc|page=376
|text=... these Machines ... must be the Work of one, who knew what he was '''about'''. And what is it, to work, and know what one is '''about'''? Tis to have an Idea of what one is doing; to possess A FORM INTERNAL, correspondent to the EXTERNAL,{{nb...}}}}
#*: And he said unto them, How is it that ye sought me? wist ye not that I must be '''about''' my Father's business?
#* '''2013''' March 14, ''{{w|Parks and Recreation}}'', season 5, episode 16, ''Bailout'':
#*: RON: I know what I’m '''about''', son.
#* {{quote-book|en|date=2018-02-07|author=Ana Vega|title=Noonity|publisher=Ana Vega|page=62
|text=I really want to know what he's '''about''', so I've arranged a date with him to hear him out.}}
# Within or in the [[immediate]] [[neighborhood]] of; in [[contiguity]] or [[proximity]] to; near, as to place. {{defdate|from ca. 1350–1470}}<ref name=SOED/>
#: {{ux|en|I can’t find my reading glasses, but they must be somewhere '''about''' the house.}}
#: {{ux|en|John’s in the garden, probably somewhere '''about''' the woodshed.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1777|author=Edward Ledwich|title=Antiquitates Sarisburienses: Or, The History and Antiquities of Old and New Sarum|page=7
|text=Carausius was born of mean parentage '''about''' Cleves in Germany, he rose in the Army by his bravery, and was appointed [...] Governor of Bononia or Bolougne in France, and Admiral {{nb...}}}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1851|author=J. H. Clark|title=The Songs of the Seasons, and Wild Flowers of the Months: Or, the British Wild Flowers Familiarly Described Under the Months in which They Bloom and the Localities in which They Grow|page=53
|text=The Saffron Crocus (''C. sativus'') grows in meadows '''about''' Essex, where it is cultivated for its fragrant stigmas, which constitute saffron.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1864|title=Zoologist: A Monthly Journal of Natural History|page=9108
|text=... small dipterous insects, which are abundant '''about''' the heaps of sea-weed.}}
#* <!--OED assigns this to "around", but it's not in a circle around or on all sides of: it seems to fit better here --> {{quote-book|en|year=1868|author=William Rossiter|title=The Elements of Plane and Spherical Trigonometry|page=14
|text={{...}} if there be any number of equiangular triangles, the sides '''about''' the equal angles are proportionals.}}
# On or near (one’s person). {{defdate|from ca. 1350–1470}}<ref name=SOED/>
#: {{ux|en|I had no weapon '''about''' me but a stick.}}
#: {{ux|en|The policy covers all belongings and other personal things that somebody can carry '''about''' them.}}
#* {{RQ:Bulwer-Lytton Ernest Maltravers|volume=I|chapter=|page=16|passage=At this assurance the traveller rose, and approached Alice softly. He drew away her hands from her face, when she said gently, "Have you much money '''about''' you?" / "Oh the mercenary baggage!" said the traveller to himself; and then replied aloud, "Why, pretty one?—Do you sell your kisses so high, then?"}}
## {{lb|en|figurative}} Attached as an attribute to; in the makeup of, or at the command of. {{defdate|from ca. 1350–1470}}<ref name=SOED/>
##: {{ux|en|He [[have one's wits about one|has his wits '''about''' him]].}}
##: {{ux|en|There was an air of confidence '''about''' the woman.}}
##* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=2|passage=Sunning himself on the board steps, I saw for the first time Mr. Farquhar Fenelon Cooke.{{...}}A silver snaffle on a heavy leather watch guard which connected the pockets of his corduroy waistcoat, together with a huge gold stirrup in his Ascot tie, sufficiently proclaimed his tastes. {{...}} But withal there was a perceptible acumen '''about''' the man which was puzzling in the extreme.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1953|author=Oliver Wendell Holmes (Jr.)|title=Holmes-Laski Letters: 1926-1935
|text=And there is a mature wisdom '''about''' him which, without being new, is newly refreshed. I did not know how profoundly my emotional loyalties were engaged to him until these days. Our plans are simple. We stay here until Thursday; then Amherst{{nb...}}}}
##* {{quote-book|en|date=2017-11-11|author=Linn Edwards|title=Food Frenzy|publisher=JMS Books LLC|isbn=9781634864886
|text=... there was a mature air '''about''' him that also suggested vacationing professional. He wore a button-down, collared shirt open a few more interesting buttons than most, revealing a small spatter of blondish-reddish hair on a broad chest{{nb...}}}}

====Usage notes====
* {{sense|Indicates that something will happen very soon}} In modern English, always followed by an infinitive that begins with ''to'' ("I am about to bathe"); see ''[[about to]]''. In the past, it was possible to instead follow the ''about'' with the present participle ("I am about swimming"), but this format is no longer used or widely understood.
* {{sense|concerning}} Used as a function word to indicate what is dealt with as the object of thought, feeling, or action.

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To draw or let out wholly; to [[drain]] completely.

#: {{ux|en|I '''exhausted''' my strength walking up the hill.}}

#: {{ux|en|The marathon '''exhausted''' me.}}

|text=It is a branch that climbs for 11½ miles into the picturesque Wealden hills until, apparently '''exhausted''' by the effort, it terminates a mile short of the village of Hawkhurst.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[discuss]] thoroughly or completely.
#: {{ux|en|That subject has already been '''exhausted'''.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|chemistry}} To subject to the action of various [[solvent]]s in order to remove all [[soluble]] substances or extractives.

|text=Infections can be reduced further if outside air is '''exhausted''' after a single use, rather than re-circulated.}}

|text=Steam from both high pressure cylinders '''exhausts''' through the respective receiver pipes into cylinders.}}

===Etymology===
{{etymon|en|:bor|fr:téléphone<id:telephone>|id=device}}
The {{lg|noun}} is derived from {{affix|en|tele-|pos1={{lg|prefix}} meaning ‘from a distance’|-phone|pos2={{lg|suffix}} denoting a device which makes a sound}}, modelled after {{cog|de|Telephon|t=early apparatus converting sound into electrical signals}} {{qualifier|dated}} (now {{cog|de|Telefon}}).<ref name="OED">{{R:OED Online|pos=n|id=2015603579|date=September 2025|nodot=1}}; {{R:Lexico|pos=n}}</ref> The word was first used to refer to the modern device in 1876 by the Scottish-born Canadian-American engineer {{w|Alexander Graham Bell}} (1847–1922).

The prefix {{m|en||tele-}} is ultimately derived from {{der|en|grc|τῆλε|t=afar, far away, far off}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*kʷelh₁-|t=to turn end-over-end; to revolve around; hence, to dwell, sojourn}}.<ref>{{R:OED Online|entry=tele-|pos=''comb. form''|noformat=1|id=3978633267|date=December 2025|nodot=1}}; {{R:Lexico|entry=tele-}}</ref> The suffix {{m|en||-phone}} is ultimately from {{der|en|grc|φωνή|t=sound; voice}},<ref>{{R:OED Online|entry=-phone|pos=''comb. form''|noformat=1|id=2891556446|date=December 2024|nodot=1}}; {{R:Lexico|entry=-phone}}</ref> and {{der|en|ine-pro|*bʰeh₂-|t=to say; to speak}}.

{{senseno|en|Q36764|uc=1}} (“system of communication using musical notes”) is borrowed from {{bor|en|fr|téléphone|t=kind of megaphone; system of communication using musical notes}}.<ref name="OED"/>

The {{lg|verb}} is derived from the noun.<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=v|id=1448846986|date=September 2025|nodot=1}}; {{R:Lexico|pos=v}}</ref>

=====Usage notes=====
* With ''did'' as an [[Appendix:Glossary#auxiliary|auxiliary verb]] (as in the negative and interrogative), '''{{m|en|use to}}''' is considered standard in American English (e.g., ''Did you use to walk to school?''; ''He didn't use to behave that way!''; ''It's hard to drive without power steering, did people just use to be stronger?'').<ref name=mw>[https://www.merriam-webster.com/words-at-play/is-it-used-to-or-use-to Merriam-Webster: Is It 'Used To' or 'Use To'?]</ref> In other situations, such as ''I use to go to the fair every year'', it is considered an error to not write the past tense form ''used to'', which is caused by the two forms sounding nearly or exactly the same.<ref name=mw/>
* The negative may be formed as ''used to not'' or ''used not to'' (''[[usen't to]], [[usedn't to]]''), ''did not use to'' (''didn't use to'').<!-- [https://www.adaptingaccents.com/single-post/didnt-used-to https://www.adaptingaccents.com/single-post/didnt-used-to/], [http://www.dailywritingtips.com/addendum-on-used-to-vs-use-to/], [http://virtuallinguist.typepad.com/the_virtual_linguist/2008/10/snowclone-and-bad-grammar-at-clapham-junction-station.html], [http://www.quora.com/Is-use-to-or-used-to-poor-grammar] -->
* The interrogative is constructed like ''did [subject] use to...?'' or ''used [subject] to...?'', varying by region and era.
* The versions ''did not use'''d''' to'' (''didn't use'''d''' to''), or, in questions, ''did [subject] use'''d''' to ...?'' are often seen and may be crowding out the versions with ''use to'', but are nevertheless generally considered non-standard.<ref name=mw/><ref name="RoutlegdeSG">Stewart Clark, Graham Pointon, ''The Routledge Student Guide to English Usage: A guide to academic writing for students'' (2016, Routledge, {{ISBN|9781317391173}}), page 296: "In questions, use ''Did he use to go to Cardiff?'' rather than ''Did he used to go to Cardiff?'' This second version is clearly non-standard. The same applies to negatives: ''He did not use to play football'' is recommended usage, but ''He did not used to play football'' is non-standard. Note that the alternative ''He used not to play football on Sundays'' is correct usage, but too formal for most contexts."</ref>
* When it is not necessary to include the following verb, it is usual in some regions to use the verb {{m|en|do}} as a stand-in (''he works harder than he used to do''), whereas in others it is usual to use no verb at all (''he works harder than he used to'').
* The form {{m|en|usedst to}} is used with {{m|en|thou}}.

Reliable sources (such as Oxford, M-W, AHDictionary, etc.) acknowledge this debate, then conclude that more recently this usage of "due to" is widely, although perhaps not entirely, acceptable. Compare also the disjunctive use of ''[[based on#Preposition|based on]]''. [https://ahdictionary.com/word/search.html?q=due+to]

===Preposition===
{{en-head|prep}}

# [[regarding|Regarding]]; [[about]]; [[concerning]].
#: {{ux|en|I can't teach that class today: I'm sick. '''As for''' the rest of the teachers, they are still on leave.}}
#: {{ux|en|'''As for''' you, we believe in you.}}
#* {{RQ:Orwell Animal Farm|3
|passage=''' As for''' the pigs, they could already read and write perfectly.}}

====Usage notes====
* ''As for'' is almost always put at the beginning of a sentence.

====Synonyms====
* {{l|en|as to}}, {{l|en|apropos}}; See also [[Thesaurus:about]]
